analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: The Fight for Capital, Samsung and TSMC Lower After Numbers, Bank Earnings Preview, Equity Capital Markets in 3Q26
key_insights: Nelson Armbrust argues a bigger issue is developing: post-GFC abundant savings and low rates are ending, while sovereign financing needs and AI capex demand for capital are both enormous, so crowding out is potentially immense.
SpaceX is reported seeking $40bn and Broadcom is reportedly exploring more than $50bn of financing. Armbrust cites both as evidence of heavy private-sector capital demand.

If scarce compute can generate 20-30% compounding IRRs, borrowers will pay high single digit rates to build it. That strains consumers, small businesses and governments built for cheap capital, and may help explain why real yields are not falling.

Credit spreads remain relatively contained because all-in yields look attractive to investors. Armbrust sees two outcomes: AI becomes self-financing from organic cash flow, which makes the next hyperscaler earnings important, or capital is rationed elsewhere and weaker parts of the economy break. CCC spreads may already show the beginning of that.
Samsung preliminary operating profit came in slightly below the Street. 005930 KS traded -3% in Korea, Kospi fell 260bps, and Korea is lower in 6 of 8 sessions.
TSM was -1.5% pre-market after a 'solid' Q3 and September sales. Q3 sales are roughly 50% higher YoY and ahead of expectations.

Armbrust says underlying demand at Samsung and TSMC is exceptionally strong. Samsung's operating profit is ₩107.4tn, and the weak stock reactions reflect expectations that were too high. Samsung smartphones are being squeezed by higher memory costs.

LG Electronics is a negative read-through: earnings disappointed despite revenue growth, with logistics and input costs an increasing burden. Armbrust says outside AI the broader corporate picture is getting more complicated.

The desk's bank earnings preview focus areas are capital markets trading normalization after a strong 2Q26, whether 3Q26 IB weakness was an air pocket, NII under a sharp rise in rates and a more hawkish forward curve, and deposit costs and deposit beta lag for 4Q26 NIMs.

Further bank preview focus areas are loan growth durability at higher rates, expense levers, and capital deployment. Less excess capital, strong loan growth and higher rates hitting AOCI could mean more buyback pauses at regionals (similar to USB) or slower buybacks at money centers.
Credit is benign going into prints, which supports possible reserve releases. The desk is watching whether the rate move creates early stress, with focus on multifamily CRE.
The desk also flags consumer health under higher oil prices and rates, and what agentic AI means for deposits, funding costs, profitability and customer growth.

Desk positioning scorecard: BAC saw a significant sentiment change at the mid-quarter conference. PGR is viewed differently on agentic AI positioning. SCHW has vocal bulls and bears. TRV is debated, with long-only investors leaning bullish and hedge funds leaning bearish.
Global ECM issuance YTD is $856bn (+60% YoY), the highest YTD level excluding 2021. Americas is $514bn (+90%), EMEA $113bn (+15%), APAC $229bn (+40%). Q3 issuance was $271bn (+35% YoY).

Global IPO issuance YTD is $280bn (+174% YoY) across 499 offerings, the strongest since 2021. Americas is $200bn (+264%), EMEA $17bn (+13%), APAC $62bn (+94%). GS is involved in about 50% of global IPO volume and led 35 IPOs.

Primary issuance YTD is $481bn (+118% YoY), with north of 50% of primary volume used to fund AI capex. Sponsor ECM is $122bn (+10%) across 222 offerings. Convertible issuance is $200bn across 250 offerings (+65% YoY), on pace for another record, about 70% Americas.

Investors view the mid-term elections as a potential clearing event. Since 1974 markets have a median -3.5% in the month before mid-terms and a median +6.5% in the four months after, which GS says sets up well for ECM into year-end.

earnings_insights: Samsung preliminary operating profit of ₩107.4tn (reported) was slightly below Street expectations. Smartphones were squeezed by higher memory costs.
TSMC Q3 sales (reported) are roughly 50% higher YoY and ahead of expectations. The September sales figure was also reported as solid.
LG Electronics earnings (reported) disappointed despite revenue growth, with logistics and input costs an increasing burden.

Bank Q3 earnings preview: capital markets trading after a strong 2Q26 and whether 3Q26 IB was an air pocket, NII, deposit costs, loan growth, expenses, capital and buybacks, credit (reserve releases possible), consumer, and agentic AI.
risk_factors: Crowding out of capital by sovereign financing needs and AI capex, with real yields staying high.
Weaker parts of the economy breaking if capital is rationed, with early signs possible in CCC spreads.
Higher rates and oil prices weighing on consumers and bank credit, with multifamily CRE a focus.
Higher rates hitting AOCI and constraining bank capital deployment, with more buyback pauses possible.
Rising logistics and input costs outside AI, as shown by LG Electronics.
Markets historically underperform in the month before mid-term elections (median -3.5% since 1974).

Korea is lower in 6 of 8 sessions, and Kospi fell 260bps on the Samsung print.

tension_points.bull_case: Scarce compute can generate 20-30% compounding IRRs, and AI may generate enough organic cash flow to become self-financing, which makes the next hyperscaler earnings important.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital is rationed elsewhere and the weaker parts of the economy begin to break, with early signs possibly in CCC spreads. Heavy AI financing crowds out consumers, small businesses and governments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next hyperscaler earnings showing whether AI becomes self-financing from organic cash flow.
